articles.title: Home Assistant shows where an automation stopped
articles.dek: Automation traces distinguish completed steps, errors and paths that never finished.
body: Home Assistant’s automation and script traces make it easier to find where a routine stopped. Their flow chart shows the actual trigger, condition and action icons, highlights the path taken in green and marks errors on the steps that contain them.

Paths beyond an unfinished branch stop appearing as though they completed. Repeat counts sit on the repeat step itself, while distinct wait icons and grouped conditions give complex automations more recognizable landmarks.

pullRequests.title: Render real trigger/condition/action icons and unfinished branch state in trace graph
Refresh trace graph primitives to match automation editor

articles.title: Home Assistant protects utility energy history from false drops
articles.dek: Opower skips incomplete updates that could corrupt recorded consumption and export totals.
body: Home Assistant protects Opower energy history from updates that can make a day’s consumption or export suddenly plunge below zero. When the utility temporarily supplies no readings at the expected detail level, the integration skips that update instead of replacing finer records with daily or billing-period totals.

Contributor tronikos found the problem on a PG&E account where recorded consumption dropped by 278 kWh and returned energy by 259 kWh in one day. A less detailed update could disturb the running totals used by later updates, producing the false drop.
The correction prevents new damage. It does not repair statistics already written with the conflicting totals.

pullRequests.title: Don't write coarser Opower statistics over finer ones

articles.title: Home Assistant offers notification actions after a tap
articles.dek: An optional iPhone setting reveals the choices without requiring a press and hold.
body: Home Assistant’s iPhone app gains a “Show actions when tapped” setting for actionable notifications. With it enabled, tapping a notification presents its choices in an alert instead of requiring the press-and-hold gesture normally used to reveal them.
The setting starts off. Text-response actions first ask for the reply, while notifications already configured to open a link, entity, shortcut or command keep their existing tap behavior.

pullRequests.title: Show notification actions when a notification is tapped

articles.title: Home Assistant checks Bosch windows and controls alarm exceptions
articles.dek: A count of open doors and windows joins switches for excluding compatible contacts from the armed alarm.
body: Bosch Smart Home households gain a single Home Assistant reading for doors and windows left open, alongside controls for intentionally excluding a compatible contact from the intrusion alarm. The summary counts open doors, windows and other openings and includes their names.

For Door/Window Contact II devices, separate switches control whether a contact is bypassed and whether that exception stays active indefinitely. This exposes the controller’s existing ability to leave a window open without that contact triggering the armed alarm.

articles.title: Home Assistant chooses a speed for each Curtain 3 movement
articles.dek: SwitchBot’s normal and silent modes can be selected for opening, closing or moving to a position.
body: Home Assistant lets an automation choose normal or silent movement for each SwitchBot Curtain 3 command. The requested speed overrides the curtain’s configured default for that opening, closing or position change.
The speed controls are limited to Curtain 3, which supports the command. Older curtain models keep their existing behavior, and commands without a speed choice continue to use the configured default.

articles.title: Home Assistant disables Linode and Tank Utility integrations
articles.dek: Unmaintained libraries prevent the two integrations from starting with updated Python packaging.
body: Home Assistant disables its Linode and Tank Utility integrations because their supporting libraries no longer work with current Python packaging. Affected users can remove them from their configuration when adopting the change.

The libraries were last released in 2018 and 2023 respectively. Maintained replacements or updates could make it possible to restore the integrations; the change does not provide an alternative connection.

pullRequests.title: Unpin setuptools and disable the linode and tank_utility integrations

articles.title: Keep the old password for ESPHome’s first encrypted-update upgrade
articles.dek: Keep the update password while installing 2026.9.0 before switching an existing device to encrypted updates.
body: Makers moving an existing ESPHome device from password-protected updates to encryption need to keep the current update password in its configuration while first installing 2026.9.0. Removing it before that installation makes the update fail.
J. Nick Koston makes that sequence explicit in the release checklist and firmware-update guide, which previously did not clearly state that the password must stay for the first installation.

pullRequests.title: [ota] Document the password to encryption migration

articles.title: INDI Allsky adds sky and camera readings to Home Assistant
articles.dek: Star counts, sky brightness, exposure and sensor temperature extend the recent camera integration.
body: People using INDI Allsky gain Home Assistant readings alongside their sky-camera snapshots. The integration adds star counts, sky-brightness measurements, exposure and sensor temperature, making information from the camera available to dashboards and automations.
Hamish extends the image-only integration reported on September 16. Additional readings for camera binning mode, filename and gain start disabled.

articles.title: Home Assistant stops Todoist appointments occupying a full day
articles.dek: Tasks with a due time receive a 30-minute calendar slot; date-only tasks stay all-day events.
body: Home Assistant gives a Todoist task with a due time a default calendar duration of 30 minutes instead of 24 hours. Tasks with only a date remain all-day events.
Andre Faria makes a first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the correction. It also prevents a boundary between consecutive calendar queries from repeating the same event.

pullRequests.title: Fix Todoist timed calendar event duration

articles.title: Home Assistant stops calendar cards overwhelming older browsers
articles.dek: A failed timezone calculation no longer starts an immediate, repeating refresh.
body: A Home Assistant calendar card could make the system unresponsive in older Chromium and Safari browsers by repeatedly subscribing to every calendar. A timezone format those browsers do not understand produced an invalid refresh delay, turning the planned midnight update into an immediate loop.
The card only schedules that refresh when the delay is valid and positive. The safeguard stops the runaway requests; it does not add the missing timezone-format support to those browsers.

pullRequests.title: Fix calendar card refresh loop on browsers without Intl longOffset support
